page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.16xlarge is a high-frequency instance type powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY CPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. Managed under a KVM hypervisor, this server configures 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. It provides a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps.

The hardware configuration balances substantial multi-core compute capability with standard memory density per core, supported by elevated CPU base clock speeds. It features no local NVMe or SSD storage and lacks hardware accelerators such as GPUs. Consequently, persistent storage operations rely entirely on network-attached volumes. Network capabilities support up to 20 Gbps of baseline throughput.

From a resource density and resource allocation perspective, the server delivers high vCPU capacity and elevated clock frequencies without allocating excessive memory per thread. This offers qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out parallel tasks and web infrastructure requiring high core counts without paying for larger memory pools. It is suited for general-purpose application workloads, CI/CD build execution, batch processing, and high-throughput application servers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud server powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor on the x86_64 architecture under KVM hypervisor management. The server features 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced resource allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Network connectivity delivers a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps. The instance omits attached local storage and hardware GPU acceleration, requiring external network storage for persistent disk operations. With high CPU clock speeds and substantial parallel processing capacity, the hardware profile offers qualitative efficiency for compute-intensive general workloads, high-concurrency web services, continuous integration execution pipelines, and distributed application backends that do not require dedicated local storage arrays or expanded memory ratios.
